However, when Hadhrat Umar (RA) appointed Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) as governor of Madaa'in, he wrote the following in his letter of appointment: "Listen to him, obey him and give him whatever he asks you for."
Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) then left Hadhrat Umar (RA) with a donkey fitted with a carriage to carry his goods. When Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) arrived in Madaa'in and was received by the people of the area and the local farmers, he was sitting on the carriage with a piece of bread and a bone with some meat in his hand. After reading out to them the letter of appointment, the people submitted, "You may ask us whatever you want." Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "All I ask for is some food to eat and fodder for this donkey as long as I am with you." After staying there for some time, Hadhrat Umar (RA) sent for him to return. Upon receiving the news that Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) was approaching (Madinah), Hadhrat Umar (RA) hid himself beside the road at a place where he would not be seen. When he saw Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) return in exactly the same condition he had left in, Hadhrat Umar (RA) came out of his hiding place and embraced Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) saying, "You are my brother and I am yours."[^1]

Hadhrat Ibn Seereen narrates, "When Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) arrived in Madaa'in, he arrived riding atop a carriage mounted on his donkey. He was eating a piece of bread with a bone with some meat." A narration of Hadhrat Talha bin Musarrif adds that at the time, Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA)'s legs were dangling on the side of the donkey.[^2]
The Humility of Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdullaah (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA)

Hadhrat Sulaym bin Abu Hudhayl says, "I mended clothes by the door of Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdullaah (RA). Whenever he came out of his house and mounted his mule, he would take his slave along with him on the animal."[^3]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) was once passing through the marketplace carrying a bundle of wood when someone said to him, "What makes you do this when Allaah has freed you from it (you can always get someone else to do it for you)?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) replied, "I wish to ward off pride because I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'The person in whose heart is an iota of pride will not enter Jannah."[^4]
